lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Apr 2021 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; the findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Wrote the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Leveraged data-driven insights and advanced analytics to unlock actionable value for urban mobility stakeholders.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- 9,000 handwritten visit logs were cleaned into a single table and repeat visitors were matched, so the pantry had its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Check that the profile link works and leads to a complete, current profile.
Add a project portfolio link only if it provides useful evidence of your work.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for most U.S. applications.
items.because: They are not needed to assess qualifications and can introduce bias.

items.says: Make the date and location formatting consistent with the rest of the resume.
Clarify whether the repeat-purchase increase can be attributed to the dashboard or retargeting.
items.because: The increase may have occurred afterward without being caused by them.

items.says: Specify whether two hours is the new total reporting time or the remaining manual work.
items.because: That distinction makes the improvement easier to assess.

items.says: The null check for customers without orders is on the wrong table’s column.
items.because: It must check a column from the orders table, not the customer name.

items.says: Separate your actions from the campaign-attribution outcome more clearly.
items.because: The opening construction is hard to follow.

items.says: Check whether “dbt-style” accurately describes the modeling work.
items.because: The wording should not imply you used dbt if you did not.

items.says: Identify the business area the funded recommendations concerned, if possible.
items.because: It would give the impact context.

items.says: Clarify the period or baseline for halving ad hoc requests, if available.
Stopping the A/B test at the first daily p-value below 0.05 is not sound statistical practice.
items.because: That stopping rule inflates the false-positive risk.

items.says: Be prepared to support the connection between the findings, staffing change and hold-time reduction.
Clarify how query errors were measured and over what period, if available.
Narrow the bullet to the automation and its monthly saving.
items.because: The unrelated duties obscure the achievement and make the bullet difficult to scan.

items.says: Remove the “Leveraged data-driven insights” bullet.
items.because: It gives no specific action, method or result.

items.says: The stated 50% reduction is incorrect; 300 to 200 is a 33% reduction.
Make clear the reduction came from a historical replay or simulation.
items.because: It was not an observed operational improvement.

items.says: Calling the change from 60% to 75% an unqualified “15%” is inaccurate.
items.because: It is 15 percentage points or a 25% relative increase.

items.says: Specify what counts as a forecast “hit.”
Keep “Present” only if the project is still active.
Check that the 50-to-20-minute comparison uses comparable Saturday periods.
Change the passive opening to make your contribution immediately clear.
Explain how household matching was validated, if possible.
items.because: That affects confidence in the unique-household count.

items.says: Consider naming a specific dashboard platform or dbt if you actually used them.
items.because: Those tools are evidenced in the bullets.

items.says: Show in the experience bullets where you applied data-quality checks and metric design.
items.because: Those skills will carry more weight with examples.
